hook: Betaine lowered urine glycoasparagines by 68.6% in children with a rare lysosomal storage disease.
hook_turn: in children with a rare lysosomal storage disease.

readout.label: Drop in urine glycoasparagines on treatment

summary: Aspartylglucosaminuria causes progressive cognitive decline, and no treatment targets it. In an open-label trial of 21 Finnish patients over 48 months, the drug Cystadane (betaine) cut a urine disease marker and appeared safe. There was no control group and no evidence yet that it slows cognitive decline.
title: Pharmacological chaperone treatment with Cystadane in aspartylglucosaminuria: an open-label, phase Ib/II trial.
